Trasadasyu
------------------------------------------
He was the son of the king पुरुकुत्स and grandson of the famous emperor मान्धातृ of the solar race. He got this name since the दस्युस् (robbers and enemies) used to quake in fear (tras = to be afraid) before him. Once the sage अगस्त्य approached him for money. Since he did not have it at that time, he suggested that the sage, along with two more kings—Śrutarva and Bradhnāśva, who had come with him—approach इल्वल, a rich and powerful dānava (belonging to the race of demons).
When अगस्त्य met him, इल्वल realised his greatness and gave him all the money he needed.
See AGASTYA and ILVALA also.

trāṭaka
------------------------------------------
It is the fifth of the षट्कर्मस् (six haṭhayogic practices meant to purify the body). It consists in gazing at any small object without winking until tears begin to flow. This practice is supposed to confer clairvoyant powers apart from curing all diseases of the eyes (Gheraṇḍa Saṁhitā 1.53, 54).
See ṢAṬKARMAS also.
